fields.description:
## Context
Legacy failure handling counts low-level physical noise (nested per-call retries) and has no endpoint-failure fuse that distinguishes an exhausted logical operation from its physical attempts; the only breaker today is the blast-radius mass-mutation guard `classify.check_blast_radius`, a different concern that is retained. The approved new scoped fuse must stop only demonstrably unhealthy scopes without terminating work that historical jobs completed.

## Outcome
Implement an endpoint/provider finite-pass fuse over normalized coordinator outcomes. Endpoint opens after three consecutive eligible exhausted logical outcomes across at least two tickets; provider additionally requires the failing outcomes to span >=2 distinct endpoints of the same provider. Matching success resets consecutive state.

## Plan
1. Count only exhausted logical outcomes eligible under the failure policy. Never count physical attempts, recovered warnings, permanent failures, ticket-local 404s, or opaque diagnostic text.
2. Track endpoint consecutive outcomes and distinct tickets. Track provider scope only when failures span >=2 distinct endpoints of the same provider.
3. Reset matching consecutive state on success; independent scopes retain their own state and continue.
4. Preserve direct authoritative credential, configuration, quota, rate, issue, endpoint, tenant, provider, and global stop/defer behavior without inferring scope from text.
5. When open, return explicit scope/reason/`retry_not_before` metadata; do not execute matching remaining plans.

## Testing
Sequence tables pin threshold boundaries, exclusions, reset, two-ticket / two-distinct-endpoint requirements, and independent scopes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Endpoint fuse opens only after three consecutive eligible exhausted outcomes across at least two tickets.
- [ ] Provider fuse additionally requires the failing outcomes to span >=2 distinct endpoints of the same provider.
- [ ] A matching success resets the consecutive state.
- [ ] Physical attempts, recovered warnings, permanent failures, ticket-local 404s, and opaque diagnostics never increment inferred counters.
- [ ] Independent scopes continue when another scope opens.
- [ ] Open-fuse outcomes include exact scope, reason, and `retry_not_before`.

## Out of scope
Production routing, batch tallies, and historical replay integration.
## Fuse scope, eligibility & counter semantics (grounds E2/G6)
No new "family" concept — grounded entirely in existing types and the S3 T1 coordinator (now landed).
- **Endpoint / provider.** *Endpoint* = one concrete provider instance an op is dispatched to (a single Jira base URL/site), the unit `operation_outcome.FailureScope.endpoint` already denotes; *provider* = the vendor behind >=1 endpoints (`FailureScope.provider`).
- **Attribution.** `coordinator.TicketOutcome` carries `identity`, `disposition`, `failure_scope` but no endpoint id; the `(provider, endpoint)` identity for an outcome is resolved from the coordinator's `locate(identity)` binding mapping (the per-ticket binding it dispatched against). The fuse keys inferred counters off that resolved identity, NEVER off diagnostic text. A direct authoritative `failure_scope` of endpoint/tenant/provider/global still stops that scope immediately (step 4), independent of the inferred counter.
- **Eligible exhausted outcome** — keyed off **budget-exhaustion provenance, not the disposition value**. The coordinator drives every transient retry through the shared per-op `retry_budget.RetryBudget`; an adapter first-attempt transient (`request_count=1`, `invocation_count=1`, `cumulative_sleep_ms=0`) is absorbed inside that retry loop and is never a pass outcome. An op is eligible only when the shared budget itself caps it: `plan_next_retry` returns `action="exhausted"` (MAX_INVOCATIONS) -> `exhausted_transient`, or `action="defer"` (would exceed `MAX_CUMULATIVE_SLEEP_MS` before MAX_INVOCATIONS) -> terminal `retryable_deferred` with `retry_not_before` and a consumed allowance (`invocation_count>1` or `cumulative_sleep_ms` at cap) — the slow/rate-limited mode that never surfaces `exhausted_transient`. The mid-loop `decide_replay(old_conclusive, budget_remaining=True)` (`replay=True`) is not a pass outcome. **Excluded**: `commit_unknown` (opaque/replay-forbidden), `recovered`, `already_satisfied`, `permanent_failure`, ticket-local 404, raw physical attempts, and any `retryable_deferred` the shared budget did not itself produce at its cap.
- **Counter durability/order.** Per-pass, in-memory, per-scope; zeroed each `reconcile.py::reconcile_once(pass_id)` pass (no durable cross-pass state, consistent with S2's fresh Observation/version). "Consecutive" is per-scope over the coordinator's deterministic dependency-ordered execution; other scopes' interleaved outcomes neither increment nor reset a scope's counter (independent scopes continue). A same-scope success (`applied`/`recovered`/`already_satisfied`) resets that scope to zero.

## Impacted sites (existing seams this change touches)
- `coordinator.py` (landed S3 T1) — `TicketOutcome`/`CoordinationReport.outcome_for`/`coordinate(...)` supply per-outcome `(identity, disposition, failure_scope)`; `locate(identity)` binding resolves the `(provider, endpoint)` identity. The fuse consumes these; `coordinate` gains fuse-defer wiring additively.
- `failure_policy.py` (landed S3 T1, 162 LOC) — `bucket_for` / `is_success` / `is_broad_scope` / `BROAD_SCOPES`; extended with the fuse-eligible-outcome predicate (budget-exhaustion provenance above). Watch 800-LOC cap.
- `retry_budget.py` — `plan_next_retry` `action in {exhausted, defer}` is the eligibility provenance; consumed read-only.
- `operation_outcome.py` — `Disposition` / `FailureScope` vocab, consumed unchanged.
- `pass_fuse.py` (new) — the per-pass scoped fuse state machine and open/defer decision.
